newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal on standby to fly nationals from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Portugal on standby to fly nationals from Zaire.

text.p: Portugal is on standby to evacuate up to 700 nationals from the Zairean capital Kinshasa on military aircraft, a spokesman said on Monday.
Rebels opposing President Mobutu Sese Seko were advancing down the road to Kinshasa. U.S. officials said the rebels led by Laurent Kabila could enter the city within two days.

"The emergency plan can be activated at three hours' notice and would follow a signal from the Portuguese ambassador," the Portuguese official, who asked not to be identified, said. "It would take place in cooperation with other countries," he added.

Portuguese nationals, mainly businessmen and their families, would be transported from designated sites to their embassy and then flown to Brazzaville. Some 15 Portuguese special forces troops were guarding the embassy, the official said.

An official told the Lusa news agency late on Monday that 68 Portuguese troops were expected to fly in two C-130 military transport planes to Brazzaville on Tuesday to help protect a possible evacuation of Portuguese nationals from Zaire.
"This is a preventive measure, in case it will be necessary to reinforce the repatriation, if the situation on the ground worsens," the official said.
The United States rotated fresh Marines into Central Africa at the weekend and urged its nationals to leave Zaire.

The Marines arrived in Congo on Saturday to join French, Belgian and British troops on standby to evacuate foreign nationals from Kinshasa in the event of a battle for the teeming city or a rampage by Zaire's ragged and ill-disciplined army.
Several thousand Western nationals live in Zaire's capital, mainly citizens of France and former colonial power Belgium.
The United States has 400 nationals there, Canada 500. A U.S. spokesman said the Marines would evacuate both and possibly other nationalities.
